subject: RestoreAssist — the job-close system water-damage restoration tradies use to turn field readings into insurer-facing inspection reports.
audience: Australian water-damage restoration tradies (sole traders and small companies); secondary, insurer claims teams and assessor networks
asset_reason: ra.ts declares defaultChannel:'linkedin' and the secondary audience is insurer claims teams. Portrait and other funnel formats are exercised at /lock, not here.
category_default_avoided: Restoration-software posts in this space default to a photo of a tech in PPE beside an air mover, with a blue-gradient UI screenshot floating over it; no variation uses a person, a device mockup, a photograph or a gradient.
token_status: ra.ts declares no tokenStatus field, so it is not 'proposal' — the SKILL.md §2 STOP condition does not apply. (john-coutis is the only brand carrying tokenStatus:'proposal'.)
axis_constraint: ra.ts declares two type families — Inter (display 800 / body 400) and JetBrains Mono (500). With three directions required, typeface class cannot vary; all three boards set display in Inter 800, which is the brand's own declared display face and therefore NOT a slop tell under SKILL.md §10. The axis is varied by role and treatment instead: mono-as-header-chips (v1), mono-as-the-whole-dataset (v2), mono absent (v3). Collision judged on colour strategy, layout system and cultural reference only.

type_ramp.problem: ra.design.md's ramp is anchored to 1920x1080 video (display-xl 96px … caption 13px). Scaling it to a 1200-wide box by width (x0.625) would put caption at 8px and body at 12px — roughly six times below SKILL.md §11's legibility floor. The ramp could not be scaled; it had to be re-anchored.
type_ramp.derivation: §11's floor is stated 'on a 1080-wide canvas', so it is read as a proportion of canvas width, not an absolute: hook 88/1080 = 8.15%, smallest text 44/1080 = 4.07%. Applied to 1200 wide: hook >= 98px, ALL other text >= 49px. Cross-check against displayed size: an Instagram 1080x1440 board at 88px shows ~31.8 CSS px on a 390pt phone; a LinkedIn 1200x627 board at 98px shows ~30.6 CSS px on the same device. The two anchorings agree to within 4%.
type_ramp.consequence: A 49px floor on every element in a 627px-tall box is severely constraining: the usable height inside the 48px safe area is 531px, which is about eight text rows total. The binding design lesson is that a landscape social box forces a SHORT hook — §5 permits seven words, but at 98px a seven-word hook costs three lines and 306px, half the board. All three hooks were cut to four to six words for this reason, not for style.

gap_detail.missing-logo:ra: public/logos/ does not exist at all; ra.ts declares logos/ra/primary.svg, inverted.svg and icon.svg, none of which are present. Every board composes without a logo and identifies the brand with a caption-type eyebrow reading 'RestoreAssist' — never 'RA' (ra.ts doNot), never styled as a lock-up. The fix is to commission the asset, not to set a wordmark in type and call it the logo.
gap_detail.missing-consumer:design_runs: No design_runs table is applied and no Linear task was created. The committed index row at docs/marketing-agency/design-runs/README.md is the only consumer of this manifest.

fonts.detail: public/fonts/ra/ holds Inter-ExtraBold.woff2 (800), Inter-Regular.woff2 (400) and JetBrainsMono-Medium.woff2 (500), matching ra.ts typography exactly. All boards load them by relative file:// path. Every render returned blocked:0 and fontsFailed:[] — the design's own type is what drew.

palette_finding.claim: RA's warm earth #8A6B4E is a FIELD colour, never a text ground or a text colour; the accent #D4A574 carries text only on the navy ground.
palette_finding.evidence: [VERIFIED] Measured from rendered pixels via a probe board (_probe/), not arithmetic: neutral-50 on #8A6B4E = 4.48:1 FAIL · navy on #8A6B4E = 2.81:1 FAIL · #8A6B4E on neutral-50 = 4.48:1 FAIL · neutral-500 #78716C on neutral-50 = 4.40:1 FAIL · tan #D4A574 on neutral-50 = 2.04:1 FAIL · tan on navy = 6.17:1 PASS.
palette_finding.consequence: Four of RA's seven plausible text pairs fail the §11 floor, three of them by less than 0.1 — close enough that arithmetic intuition would have passed them. Every board therefore uses warm earth only as a text-free field (v1's carbon strip, v3's wet line) and places tan only as a CTA fill with navy type. This is a design constraint of the RA palette, not a choice made by this run.

contrast_method: Measured from the rendered PNG pixels with .artifacts/design-runs/ra-job-close-system-2026-08-29-01/measure-contrast.mjs (sharp, raw RGB, WCAG 2.1 relative luminance). Per named text region the true ink and true ground are the luminance extremes — greyscale antialiasing only interpolates between them — and a 2nd/98th-percentile pair is reported alongside as a stability check. The two agreed to within 0.01 on every region, confirming each rect captured exactly one ink/ground pair. Regions are recorded per variation in regions.json.

variations.name: job-card
variations.support: Built for restoration work across Australia and New Zealand.

tokens.signature: A docket rule pair — 2px above, 1px below — bracketing the hook band, closed by a full-bleed text-free warm-earth carbon strip with a 4px tan edge

variations.why: In the rendered board the docket bracket reads and the hook lands, but the support block stops at x≈770 and leaves the quadrant beneath the CTA empty — the composition's weight sits left of its action. Navy-with-reversed-Inter is also the most category-default ground in the set.

variations.name: drying-log
variations.direction: Data-led / the moisture log as the whole composition
variations.support: Built for restoration work across Australia and New Zealand.

tokens.signature: A ruled drying-log ledger whose right-hand column is an action column, split off by a vertical hairline and holding the CTA and the SAMPLE stamp

variations.signature_rule: rows = floor((ledgerBox - headerRow) / minRowHeight), minRowHeight = 1.25 x the 4.07%-of-width text floor (61px at 1200 wide), ledgerBox measured after the hook, support and gaps are laid out. At 1200x627: ledgerBox = 531 - 102 - 20 - 24 - 130 = 255, so floor((255-60)/61) = 3 rows. Below 2 rows the ledger HIDES ITSELF and the board falls back to hook + CTA — a one-row ledger is a caption pretending to be a system. Above 8 rows it caps at 8, beyond which the falling WME column stops reading as a trend. This is the stated extremes rule PRINCIPLES.md line 3 requires.
variations.why: The rendered ledger genuinely reads as a drying log — the 24.6 → 19.1 → 14.8 fall is legible at a glance and the action column now has a real right edge. It is the most template-ready board in the set. Held back because the eye can land on the data first and read the board as a table rather than as an advertisement, and the embedded CTA is second rather than co-equal.

variations.name: sweep
variations.direction: The wet line — the taped boundary a tech marks where water stopped
variations.hook: Draw the line. Send the report.
variations.support: Built for restoration work across Australia and New Zealand.

tokens.signature: A stepped warm-earth wet-line running full-bleed across the board, dividing a navy wet field from a light dry field. RA's declared 'sweep' motion signature rendered static.

variations.signature_rule: The line sits at 59.4% of height; step depth is 7.2% of height; the riser stands one 56px gutter clear of the hook's longest line rather than at a fixed column, so it can never collide with the type at any measure. Below ~400px tall the step FLATTENS to a straight line — a step under 24px reads as a rendering artefact, not a mark. Below ~320px tall the line hides entirely and the board falls back to a flat navy field with the hook reversed out of it.
variations.why: In the rendered board the stepped earth line reads as a taped wet-line and the hook sits wholly inside the navy above it, clearing the step by 49px with the riser 56px clear of the type — the concept survived the render intact, which is the test PRINCIPLES.md line 2 sets. Its signature is a composition rather than a figure, so it does not depend on a claim (PRINCIPLES.md line 1), and it is the only direction that carries RA's own declared motion signature, so a locked template would propagate coherently into video.

template.fidelity: The template refilled at 1200x627 with the locked copy renders byte-identical (cmp) to the promoted winner PNG. The promoted board itself also re-renders byte-identical to public/marketing-agency/design-runs/ra-job-close-system-2026-08-29-01/sweep.png after the font-path rebase.
template.signature_is_executable: The §13 step-4 rule is code in the template, not prose about it: the line, step, thickness, tick and riser are all derived from the measured box, and both degradation paths were rendered and looked at rather than asserted.
corrections_made_at_lock: PORTRAIT RULE. 59.4% of height is a LANDSCAPE proportion. Carried onto 1080x1440 it stranded the tape in an empty light field with the support marooned ~400px below — two voids with the message squeezed between. On a portrait box the dry field is now sized to its content.

RISER PLACEMENT. The manifest and tokens.json said 'one 56px gutter clear of the hook's longest line rather than at a fixed column'; the board's source comment said '80.7% of width'. The pixels settle it — hook right edge 802.4, riser 968 — so 56px was the CONSTRAINT the column was checked against, not the placement. The template applies the column first and the gutter as an override.
LONE CTA. With the support empty, flex space-between put the og-image's CTA at the bottom-LEFT where the locked board puts it hard right. A single-item bottom row now justifies to flex-end.
